title: Redwood March 2026 All-hands
summary: Company all-hands covering Q1 results, product roadmap updates (Dedicated, Private, Optimize), reliability incident review, hiring update, and org priorities. Leadership answered questions on pricing, dedicated capacity, and upcoming customer pilots. Deck and recording to be shared; office hours scheduled for follow-ups.
action_items: Elena: Share all-hands deck and recording with company (due 2026-03-06)
Priya: Publish postmortem for Mar 1 outage and remediation plan (due 2026-03-08)
Owen: Post roadmap summary with feature dates and beta signups (due 2026-03-10)
Kara: Share updated hiring plan + open reqs and interview backlog (due 2026-03-12)
Marcus & Maya: Schedule kernel/quantization deep-dive office hours for infra+research teams (due 2026-03-09)
next_steps: Deck + recording will be posted to #all-hands and Confluence
Sign up for product office hours for detailed Q&A
Leads to submit roadmap feedback via the form linked in the deck
Customer success to prepare a slide with top 5 pilot customers for next all-hands
header: Date: 2026-03-05 17:00 PST | Duration: 75 minutes | Host: Elena Park | Attendees: Leadership + all employees
transcript:
[00:00] Elena: Welcome everyone, um great to see so many faces. We're gonna get started, I'm Elena, we'll run about an hour and 15. Quick agenda, business update, product, reliability, hiring and Q&A.
[00:18] Marcus: Quick update from infra side — Q1 we've seen a 28% increase in token volume week-over-week, which is great but also, uh, stressful for some of our autoscaling paths.
[00:35] Priya: On Dedicated we shipped the new pool scheduler last week, so customers on reserved capacity should see more consistent p99s. There's still tuning left on burst policies.
[00:52] Owen: Product highlights — Redwood Optimize new recommendations engine is in closed beta, we have customers seeing ~20% token cost reduction with prefix caching suggestions. Beta invites are open.
[01:08] Maya: Research — quantization improvements landed for LLaMA-derived families, early perf shows 2–3x improvement on A100 for small seq lengths. Lots of caveats but promising.
[01:30] Elena: Topline business — ARR up 14% quarter-over-quarter, pilot conversions trending well. Notably, two mid-market customers moved from trial to paid Dedicated this month which helps pipeline.
[01:46] Crowd murmur / applause.
[02:00] Kara: Hiring — we are still prioritizing SRE, backend, and a couple of commercial roles. Interview funnel is tight; please refer candidates and update the referral tracker.
[02:18] Question from Slack: "What's the plan for Private (VPC/on-prem) GA?"
[02:25] Owen: We're targeting GA for core Private control plane in Q2, with an on-prem appliance pilot for 2 customers in April. There are open items on KMS integrations and audit logs.
[02:44] Marcus: On security — SOC 2 readiness is on track; we've mapped gaps and are closing them this quarter. The Mar 1 outage did exercise our incident response and we have a postmortem coming.
[03:05] Elena: Let's talk about the Mar 1 outage briefly — it affected hosted multi-tenant endpoints for about 22 minutes, root cause was a regression in the batching router that caused some KV cache thrash. Priya will publish the postmortem.
[03:30] Priya: Yeah, the regression slipped through an optimization path; fixes are deployed and we've added additional unit tests and synthetic traffic checks. Sorry for the disruption.
[03:50] Marcus: Also added more tracing and a canary for kernel selection logic to prevent similar regressions.
[04:10] Employee question: "Will pricing change because of Dedicated demand?"
[04:18] Elena: No wholesale price change planned, but we will roll out clearer guidance on pooling and batching to help customers reduce cost. We're also experimenting with volume-tiered discounts for committed capacity.
[04:40] Owen: We know customers care about latency vs cost tradeoffs; we'll publish a runbook on recommended configurations for common workloads.
[04:58] Cross-talk and a few off-mic chuckles.
[05:20] Marcus: On the tech roadmap — short term (next 6–10 weeks): kernel selection improvements, better continuous batching heuristics, and KV cache persistence for hot prefixes. Medium term: fast-failover for region outages and more model variant compatibilities.
[05:45] Maya: R&D will prioritize quantization across more model families and a small eval kit to prevent quality regressions when teams change quantization/kv cache strategies.
[06:05] Sales highlight: two mid-market wins and an enterprise pilot with a regulated healthcare customer; CS callouts on compliance were key.
[06:20] Elena: Big thanks to the CS team for running the security workshops.
[06:30] Kara: People ops — we have four new hires starting next week and a recruiting push in EMEA. Also, reminder: open PTO holiday schedule before end of month.
[06:48] Employee Q: "How should teams prioritize infra projects vs feature work?"
[06:56] Priya: Good question — leads should balance reliability sprints into every other cycle; we expect infra to be productized not just internal toil. We'll publish a guidance doc.
[07:20] Elena: Org changes — moving platform reliability under Priya's scope and creating a small runtime performance squad reporting to Marcus. This helps align kernel work and infra runbooks.
[07:40] Short applause.
[07:55] Owen: A reminder about the public benchmarks we published — please don't link customer names, use the aggregate numbers deck. We will update the benchmarks after the next round of kernel improvements.
[08:12] Employee: "Any update on international regions?"
[08:20] Elena: APAC region is planned for Q3 with cloud partners; working on compliance and partner agreements.
[08:33] Marcus: Ops note — we're adding more observability in the console: token-level latency histograms, per-route error breakdowns, and better tracing integration. Expect a beta next month.
[08:51] Maya: Also adding eval-linked regression alerts, so we can detect quality drops tied to a quantization or prompt change.
[09:10] Q&A rapid fire: various product/HR/legal micro-questions (SAML/SSO status, audit window, PTO accrual).
[10:00] Elena: Closing remarks — big thanks; focus for next quarter is Reliable Serving, Private GA, and hitting committed capacity targets. Be kind, ship, and reach out to leads.
[10:18] Elena: Ok those are the formal items — we'll post the deck and record, follow-up office hours scheduled for next Tue and Thu for product and infra deep-dives.
[10:35] Crowd chatter and the meeting winds down.
[11:00] End of recording.

Notes on transcription: typical fireflies auto-transcribe glitches — some product names mis-typed (LAMA vs LLaMA), occasional speaker label drift, filler words present.
